hints: Focus on what makes a carbon chiral, a carbon with four different groups attached and no double bonds.
Look at the two CH carbons in the middle of the chain, one bonded to NH2 and one bonded to NH, and check their four groups.
Rule out all CH2 groups and C=O groups, then confirm that both central CH carbons have four different neighbours.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for a chiral carbon**

A chiral carbon must be sp3, so single bonds only, and bonded to four different atoms or groups.

Rule to apply:
$$ \text{chiral C} = \text{C with 4 single bonds to 4 different groups} $$

**Simplify the structure of aspartame**

Write it out left to right to see each carbon clearly.

Simplified chain:
$$ \text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-CH(NH}_2\text{)-CONH-CH(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-C}_6\text{H}_5 $$

**Eliminate carbons that cannot be chiral**

All C=O carbons have a double bond, so they cannot be chiral. All $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2$ carbons have repeated H atoms, so they cannot be chiral either.

That leaves only two candidates, the two CH carbons in the centre.

**Check the left CH carbon**

This carbon is bonded to $\text{NH}_2$, H, $\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, and $\text{CONH}$.

All four groups are different, so this carbon is chiral.

**Check the right CH carbon**

This carbon is bonded to NH, H, $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{CH}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$.

All four groups are different, so this carbon is also chiral. That gives 2 chiral carbons in total.

options.A: 1 is too few. Students who choose this often spot only one of the two central CH carbons and miss the other. Both the aspartic acid part and the phenylalanine part each contribute one chiral centre.
options.B: 2 is correct. The two CH carbons, one with NH2 and one with NH, each have four different single-bonded groups and are chiral. All C=O, CH2, CH3 and phenyl carbons fail the four-different-groups test.
options.C: 3 is too many. This often comes from wrongly counting a CH2 group next to C=O or next to the phenyl ring as chiral. A CH2 has two identical H atoms, so it can never be chiral.
options.D: 4 is too many. This comes from counting both CH2 groups as chiral as well as the two true CH centres. Remember, any carbon with two H atoms or any carbon with a double bond is automatically not chiral.
